project.name: pulpe-workspace
project.description: Pulpe is a Swiss personal-budget planning application that turns reusable templates into monthly budgets, tracks actual transactions, and plans savings goals across web and iOS clients.

nodes.name: Budget Planning
nodes.summary: This domain builds reusable budget templates and turns them into monthly plans made of income, recurring, one-off, and saving forecasts. It also maintains balances when forecasts or actual operations change.

businessRules: A monthly budget belongs to a period and is generated from a template.
Forecast amounts and ending balances are encrypted before persistence.
Balance recalculation must account for forecast lines and actual transactions.
crossDomainInteractions: Transactions consume or remain outside budget lines.
Saving forecast lines can link to savings goals.
Tags and currency metadata enrich forecast lines.

nodes.name: Transaction Tracking
nodes.summary: This domain records actual income, expenses, and savings, then associates them with monthly budgets and optional forecast envelopes. It supports pointing, searching, postponing, spreading, and allocation workflows.

businessRules: A transaction belongs to a monthly budget and may be allocated to one budget line.
Transaction amounts are encrypted before persistence.
crossDomainInteractions: Saving transactions contribute to linked savings goals.
Tags and currency metadata support classification and display.

nodes.name: Savings Goals
nodes.summary: This domain defines target-based savings objectives and derives their progress from linked saving forecasts and actual contributions. It can simulate and apply future contribution plans, stop future generation, and model withdrawals.

businessRules: Target amounts and initial amounts are encrypted before persistence.
Progress is derived from linked budget lines and actual saving transactions.
Applied plans create or update future saving forecast lines.
crossDomainInteractions: Goals link to budget-template and monthly-budget saving lines.

nodes.name: Account and Financial Vault
nodes.summary: This domain authenticates users, manages profile and budgeting preferences, and protects financial data with a client key, PIN, and recovery key. It also schedules and executes account deletion after a grace period.

businessRules: Authenticated financial requests require both a valid session and client encryption key.
Recovery and PIN changes must preserve access to encrypted financial data.
Scheduled deletion observes a three-day grace period.
crossDomainInteractions: All financial domains depend on authenticated ownership and decrypted amounts.
Pay-day and currency preferences affect budget periods and amount presentation.
Account deletion removes user-owned domain data and analytics identity.

nodes.name: Financial Metadata
nodes.summary: This domain classifies financial records with reusable tags and supplies currency conversion metadata. It supports tag history and consistent display of base and foreign-currency amounts.

businessRules: Tags can be linked atomically to templates, forecasts, and transactions.
Currency conversion retains source-currency metadata alongside the base amount.
Tag history is derived from the user's financial records.
crossDomainInteractions: Budget lines and transactions consume tags and currency metadata.
User settings provide the base currency.

nodes.name: Guided Product Experience
nodes.summary: This domain helps users reach and operate the core budgeting experience through onboarding, demo data, the current-month dashboard, maintenance gating, version gating, and release notes. It coordinates platform lifecycle state around the financial domains.

businessRules: Demo sessions use isolated generated data and expire automatically.
Startup can be gated by maintenance and minimum app-version checks.
Current-month views aggregate budgets, forecasts, and transactions.
crossDomainInteractions: Onboarding seeds the first budget template.
The current-month dashboard aggregates budgets, transactions, and savings.

edges.description: Authentication, ownership, decryption, pay-day, and currency settings govern every budget operation.
Monthly budgets receive actual transactions and expose forecast envelopes for allocation.
Transaction mutations trigger budget balance recalculation.
Savings plans create and update goal-linked saving forecast lines.
Actual saving transactions contribute to linked-goal progress.
Tags and currency metadata classify and display budget forecasts.
Tags and currency metadata classify transactions and support filtered search.
Onboarding and demo flows seed budgets, while the current-month view aggregates them.
Demo generation and the current-month dashboard populate and present actual operations.
